scope: PC on-foot keyboard/mouse references. RE4 means 2023 remake; not the 2005 tank-control original. Default/reference layouts are not locally verified installed builds. Player expectations below are design inferences, not a user survey.

games.name: RDR2
games.lesson: Keep item handling and prompts readable; distinguish environmental use from combat input. Weight should come from animation without hiding the accepted input.

games.name: The Witcher 3
games.lesson: Separate a short evasive step from a long roll. Combat targeting changes movement expectations; one generic dodge is insufficient.

games.name: Elden Ring*
games.scope: Launch-era PC reference; conflicting publisher variant below
games.lesson: Target-facing combat, attack commitment and evasion need explicit states. Adopt those ideas independently of its shared dash/dodge key.

games.name: Resident Evil 4
games.lesson: Over-the-shoulder focus, quick turn and contextual traversal provide distinct modes. A dedicated parry key is not a free-jump key.

games.name: GTA V
games.lesson: Use clear transitions between locomotion, aim-strafing, cover and object/vehicle interaction. Vehicle systems are outside this lab's current scope.

hybrid.detail: Explore facing travel. Hold RMB to face camera heading and strafe. Mouse look uses browser pointer capture; first captured click does not attack.
Sprint separated from jump and dodge. Choose Hold or Toggle in Controls. Normalize diagonals; keep crouch/carry speed limits.
Walk/jog toggle. Numeric 1-4 remain explicit lab speed overrides; a finished game could use those slots for equipment.

Space preempts ground actions and crouch/seiza. Selects a vault or mantle at explicitly tagged, reachable surfaces with free landing room; otherwise jumps from approach speed. Ctrl+Space forces a normal high jump. Exact hand/foot contacts are still probes.
Alt triggers a 0.32-second evade with collision-limited world travel. Fresh movement, another action, C or Space replaces it immediately. Directional rolls and invulnerability remain unimplemented.

Single C immediately enters crouch locomotion; C C within 300 ms selects static kneeling/seiza. Movement leaves seiza into crouch. Space jumps from either with a headroom check. Prone support contacts and hold-crouch remain incomplete. C is unmodified: Ctrl+C and other Ctrl/Command browser shortcuts bypass gameplay. Ctrl+Space is the explicit high-jump exception.
Show the action and target before pressing. A carried box gets put down; otherwise use the nearest usable object. View/occlusion scoring and progress/cancel affordances remain planned.

Every LMB click starts/restarts alternating jab/cross, including the initial capture click. F kicks. Short sampled source windows replace full-clip locks; Space preempts attacks and fresh movement cancels them. Hit validation, weapon layers and upper-body movement blending remain missing.
RMB selects facing/strafe behavior, not a fictional weapon aim or held guard. B triggers the existing one-shot block.
Without a target system this recenters the camera. Actual lock acquisition, target switching and target-facing strafes need implementation.

hybrid.live: R reserved; V camera side implemented
hybrid.detail: This lab has no weapon/reload system. Reserve R now rather than training recording muscle memory there. V swaps camera side while focused.
Recording stays available without consuming the usual reload key. Original Lab preset retains R.
Esc pauses and releases mouse in Hybrid. Menus keep keyboard focus and gameplay input is suppressed.
Action rebinding, binding conflict checks, camera sensitivity/inversion and keyboard camera alternatives remain controller work. Not new animation requirements.

audit.name: Gait phase, starts/stops and pivots
audit.work: Both: metadata/controller first, then targeted motion variants.
audit.test: Walk to jog to sprint to stop, on both lead feet; turn 90 degrees and reverse 180 degrees without foot snaps. Current motion() resets phase when changing clips.

audit.name: Sustained combat-ready posture
audit.status: Game loops missing; earlier guard sources exist
missing: Guard walk and strafe in eight directions
audit.work: Reuse earlier Fight guard/footwork takes before new generation; derive proper loops and add state/interrupt rules.
audit.test: Hold focus for 10 seconds, circle and backpedal, attack and return to guard without dropping into relaxed idle.

audit.name: Real target-facing locomotion
audit.status: Ordinary strafe clips exist; target system missing
missing: Actor-local direction selection around a target
audit.work: Controller and camera first. Existing directional loops can seed the test.
audit.test: Circle a moving target clockwise/counterclockwise and retreat while facing it. A focus camera-heading strafe is not target lock.

audit.name: Short dodge versus long roll
audit.status: Short directional bursts wired; long roll set missing
audit.work: Active source windows and a 0.32-second displacement curve now drive interruptible evades. Assess their visual quality before adding directional rolls.
audit.test: Evade in each direction, then immediately move, C, punch or Space. Confirm cancellation without a second Alt press and solid-wall collision.

audit.name: Reusable airborne / fall / landing states
audit.status: Jump/fall and high-drop superhero contact layer wired; fall pose library partial
audit.work: Segment/tag existing jumps first; generate only missing recovery/fall variants.
audit.test: Jump at different approach speeds and off a ledge, land early/late, then continue in the held direction without replaying an entire jump.

audit.name: Responsive stance transitions
audit.status: Immediate crouch and double-C seiza wired; support variants partial
missing: Headroom checks across every stance exit, including prone
audit.work: Trim and tag transition windows, then controller rules; contact retakes only where needed.
audit.test: C immediately selects crouch locomotion; C C holds seiza; Space preempts either. Standing and jump exits must reject a low ceiling. Assess the short pose blend and support contacts visually.

audit.name: Carrying under real interaction conditions
audit.status: Baseline present; support and variants partial
audit.work: Both. Fix grip/contact rules and prop parenting before requesting many more clips.
audit.test: Lift, rotate, carry diagonally, stop, put down on a marked surface and interrupt safely. Record props separately: current character GLB recording excludes them.

audit.name: Action timing, buffering and safe context
audit.status: Immediate replacement / repeat attack wired; deeper context rules partial
missing: Short bounded input buffer around actual landing
Combat-specific commitment rules and damage events
View / occlusion scoring for E objects
audit.test: Alt to Space, crouch to Space, repeated LMB, punch to Space and cold-load cancellation must keep the latest input. Pickup/putdown cancellation must preserve the actual attachment event.

audit.name: Weapon aim, draw and reload
audit.work: Requires weapon props, attachment rig and animation layers as well as clips.
audit.test: Aim over either shoulder, move and reload while feet continue their gait. Do not claim an RMB focus mode supplies these animations.

audit.name: Cover and contextual traversal
audit.status: Low vault/mantle and high ledge-grab/pull-up wired; contact quality needs review
missing: Ladder mount / idle / up / down / dismount
audit.work: Explicit range/height/landing checks; high ledges add jump/catch/hang/pull-up/top-out with hand locks. Authored contact layers over generated sources, not a learned physical climbing policy. Ladders and cover remain open.
audit.test: Same action at several real obstacle heights with hands and feet staying attached. A text-prompt vault is not validated contact traversal.

audit.name: Directional reactions and ground recovery
audit.work: Repair existing body/floor contacts before multiplying variants.
audit.test: Both robots recover without armour, head or hands passing through floor or seats. Raw ground intersections remain measured in this kit.

audit.name: Remapping and readable input feedback
audit.work: Input/UI work. Requires no new mocap.
audit.test: Navigate controls with keyboard, remap E, reload and export settings, and verify prompts/menus preserve the same action semantics.

audit.name: Genre-specific expansion
audit.work: New gameplay, props and motions; not baseline locomotion requirements.
audit.test: Add only after the level and game design need that mechanic; do not copy every feature from all five games into one controller.

principles: Use a stable action vocabulary: move, sprint, jump, evade, interact, focus. Nearby keys are not evidence of identical mechanics.
Separate free exploration, focused strafing and real target lock. Camera orbit alone must not drag an idle character around.
Keep interactions explicit and targeted. Show the target before E; do not turn a harmless interaction key into an attack.
Define action timing and interruption. A clip ending and a character being ready for the next input are separate decisions.
Preserve stride phase, contacts and travel. More generated clips do not substitute for animation state metadata and collision.
Offer personal input choices. Remapping and hold/toggle options matter more than declaring C or Ctrl universally correct.
